explanation: I searched Mathlib for a declaration stating that the image of a submodule with a basis under a linear map is the span of the images of the basis vectors. The searches covered `map_eq_span`, `map_span`, `span_image`, `range_comp` and Basis/submodule/subtype combinations. The nearest hits were `Submodule.map_span` and `Submodule.span_image`, which only treat the span of a set. `Module.Basis.mem_submodule_iff` in `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Submodule.lean` uses the same `map_top`/`b.span_eq`/`map_span` argument inline but states something different. Deriving the target from `Submodule.map_span` needs the basis-spans-top step and the range manipulations, which is more than two short lines.
